issues.title: Order total is off by a cent on some orders
issues.body: `orders/total.py` sums floats and rounds with `round`, so 3 × 0.35 gives 1.05 on one order and 1.04 on another. Done when the total rounds half up, in Decimal.

issues.title: Export the orders of a month as CSV
issues.body: The shop owner needs the orders of a month as a CSV file: order, customer, total.

issues.title: Dark mode for the admin pages
issues.body: The admin pages have only a light theme.

issues.title: Rename get_invoice_total to invoice_total
issues.body:
`billing/invoice.py:4`: the function `get_invoice_total` computes a value. It does not get one. The `get_` prefix adds no information. The name `invoice_total` says the same thing in fewer words.

How it shows: only in the name. No behaviour changes.

Fix: rename `get_invoice_total` to `invoice_total`, and update each caller. Today the repository has no callers.

Out of scope for #14: the finding is in `billing`, and #14 changes only `orders`. Found in the review of the branch for #14.

issues.title: Docstring of vat says cents, but it returns euros
issues.body:
`billing/tax.py:4`: the docstring of `vat` says "Returns the VAT on amount, in cents." The function returns euros, as a `Decimal` quantized to `0.01`. Its only caller, `get_invoice_total` in `billing/invoice.py:5`, adds the result to an order total in euros.

How it shows: a reader who trusts the docstring can divide the result by 100, or multiply an input by 100. Either gives a total that is wrong by a factor of 100.

Fix: change the docstring to say that `vat` returns the VAT on `amount`, in euros, rounded to the cent.

Out of scope for #14: the finding is in `billing`, and #14 changes only `orders`. Found in the review of the branch for #14.

issues.title: sign_up treats emails that differ only in case as different accounts
issues.body:
`accounts/signup.py:4`: `sign_up` stores the email as the user typed it, and checks for an existing account with the same exact string. So `Bob@shop.test` and `bob@shop.test` sign up as two accounts.

How it shows:

```python
sign_up("Bob@shop.test", "h1")
sign_up("bob@shop.test", "h2")  # no ValueError: a second account
```

Open question before the fix: normalize the whole address (`strip()` and `lower()`), or only the domain part? RFC 5321 lets the local part be case-sensitive, but most services treat it as case-insensitive. The fix needs a test with the two addresses above.

Out of scope for #14: the finding is in `accounts`, and #14 changes only `orders`. Found in the review of the branch for #14.
